title: Hamilton and Niagara regions head to the polls to choose next municipal governments

image.caption: A polling station in Hamilton. (Saira Peesker/CBC)

items: October 26Where can you find results tonightCBC Hamilton will be reporting on results for Hamilton, Niagara, Burlington, Brantford and Norfolk here after polls close at 8 p.m. We will also be supported by the CBC Decision Desk, which will help make calls, especially when they are close. City hall in Hamilton will also be open to members of the public and media on election night. Screens outside council chambers are expected to show a live feed of the city's results website.Some of the mayoral candidates are also hosting watch parties. Rob Cooper, his campaign team, volunteers and supporters will be watching the results at the Southern Pines Golf & Country Club on 8453 Airport Rd. E. Scarlett Gillespie and her team will be at Conversate Steak and Seafood on 38 King William St. Andrea Horwath's team will be watching results and is welcoming supporters to Henry's on James, at 303 James St. N., from 8 p.m. onwards. Keanin Loomis's campaign is hosting a watch party from 7 p.m. to 10 p.m. at Bridgeworks, 200 Caroline St. N.

What issues Hamilton voters and candidates care about this yearJeffery TramI'm Jeffery Tram, a reporter with CBC Hamilton. I've been around the city today at polling stations, talking to voters.Since nominations opened on May 1, we've heard from candidates and residents about the key issues shaping this municipal election — including affordability, homelessness, property taxes, road infrastructure and local government accountability. In a CBC survey about issues that mattered this election, 636 residents responded in Hamilton — saying homelessness and encampments, property taxes and city budgets and road infrastructure and traffic were top of the list. Students at McMaster University also told us they're concerned about issues including affordability, homelessness and public transit. In our survey of candidates and at various candidate debates, we heard that many Hamiltonians are worried about the cost of living. Generally, voters and candidates have said they want elected officials to be accountable and transparent, and that they want good value for public money.

Who's running for mayor of Hamilton?Justin ChandlerGet to know the 2026 Hamilton mayoral candidatesThe stakes are high this upcoming election on Oct. 26 for Hamilton incumbent mayor Andrea Horwath, who will once again face former Hamilton Chamber of Commerce leader Keanin Loomis, after winning by a 1.7 per cent margin in 2022. Here are some of the promises four out of the 13 candidates in Hamilton are making.Hamilton's 2022 mayoral election was a nail-biter, with Andrea Horwath defeating second-place candidate Keanin Loomis by about 1,600 votes.Tonight, we're witnessing a rematch. Loomis — a chamber-of-commerce-leader turned steel-industry-association head — is taking on the longtime Hamilton politician again. They're joined on the ballot by 11 other candidates, including Rob Cooper, city councillor for Ward 8, and affordable housing advocate Scarlett Gillespie.Unsure about who you're voting for? Here's the full list of who's running and the top issues they say they'll tackle if elected. We've also reported mayoral candidates' promises about homelessness, property taxes and data centres.

Election day is here in Hamilton and NiagaraJustin ChandlerA polling station in Hamilton. (Saira Peesker/CBC)I'm Justin Chandler, a CBC Hamilton reporter here for the big day.Voters in municipalities across Ontario will choose mayors, city councillors and school board trustees to lead them for the next four years.Municipal government directly affects residents' lives. Decisions around roads, water, garbage pickup, affordable housing and property taxes are all made at city hall. In my newsroom, we'll be keeping a close eye on Hamilton's 13-candidate mayoral race. We'll also be reporting on the council and trustee races. There will be at least three new councillors in Hamilton, in wards 8, 10 and 13. My colleagues in Niagara will be watching multiple mayoral races in the region — four have no incumbent — and reporting full election results for all 12 municipalities. The 2022 municipal election in Hamilton was decided with about a third of eligible voters casting ballots. Have you voted already? There’s still some time — most stations are open until 8 p.m. The City of Hamilton has a searchable map of polling stations — this year you can vote at any polling station in your ward. You do not need a voter card, but remember to bring identification showing your name and home address.
